title: Rivers and wetlands as environments
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:16Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, River health in the basin, is about how human actions degrade rivers, while the new point describes rivers, lakes and wetlands as environments that store and filter water, support fish and birds, and link to their catchments, so it teaches a different idea.

draft.title: Rivers and wetlands as environments
card: Rivers, lakes and wetlands are inland water environments. They store water, and some of it soaks into the ground or flows on to other places.
Wetlands such as swamps and floodplains slow water down. Plants and soil trap sediment and some pollutants, so the water leaving is often cleaner.
These places give food, shelter and breeding sites for fish, frogs and waterbirds. Many birds travel long distances to breed when wetlands fill with water.
A catchment is the area of land that drains into a river or lake. What happens on that land, such as clearing or farming, can change the water that reaches it.
draft.remember: Inland water stores and filters water, supports wildlife, and is linked to its catchment.

opts: The land area that drains into a river or lake
The deepest channel running along a river bed
The wetland where a river finally meets the sea
The amount of water a dam is able to hold
a.why: A catchment is the land that drains into a river or lake, so activity on that land can affect the water. The other options describe a channel, a river's end and a dam's capacity, not the area of drained land.
a.clue: Think of the land that water runs off before it reaches the river.

b.q: Farmers in a catchment clear the trees along a creek. Soil washes into the creek and then into a wetland downstream. Which is the best explanation?
opts: The wetland is linked to the land that drains into it
The wetland makes the creek carry more soil
The wetland stores water so it cannot be changed
The soil moves because wetlands are only filters
b.why: Water and soil move from the catchment to the wetland, so changes on the land affect the water downstream. The wetland does not cause the soil to move. Filtering is one role, but it does not stop the wetland being changed.
b.clue: Which option says where the soil came from?

wants.brief: A simple labelled catchment: hills on each side, rain falling, a creek and a river running down the middle to a wetland and lake, with the catchment boundary outlined and labelled 'catchment'.
wants.why: It shows how land drains into inland water.

a.best: The land area that drains into a river or lake

b.best: The wetland is linked to the land that drains into it
